parsed.explanation: Severe-band risk. A cross-dressing/impersonation offence (Art. 266(d)) is documented as enforced against gender-nonconforming men, with 2018 sentences of 3-4 years and 2020 arrests. Digital surveillance and evidence-triggered prosecution raise the chance of being outed, and same-sex conduct is criminalised. A 2023 first-hand report describes a nonbinary visitor held, made to remove her shirt and touched by border officers, a traveller-facing exposure. Legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care are banned, and felony convictions bring mandatory deportation. Mitigators are thin: no recent enforcement is documented after July 2020, and no acceptance or working recourse appears. Prison housing is unresolved, and no violence rate is available, so no execution or trans-specific killing is established. Extrapolating from the criminalising structure and documented enforcement places this well below the elevated tier, but short of the capital-enforcement anchors.
